summary: Arcadia Health: audit log export format/fields + export cadence questions for compliance (Private/VPC)
related_github_prs: redwood-docs#869 (notes only: audit logging section to update; do not publish customer specifics)
related_confluence_pages: Confluence (internal): Private Deployments > Audit logging & exports
description:
Issue summary
Arcadia Health (Private/VPC) is onboarding as a design partner and is preparing their internal compliance checklist. They asked for a definitive list of audit log fields + export cadence options (near-real-time vs daily) and how exports are delivered (S3 vs API). They want to confirm the audit log schema supports:
- Access auditing (who did what, when)
- Request tracing (tie back to their app request IDs)
- Operational auditing for regulated workflows (retention, immutability expectations)

Customer ask (from Arcadia platform + security)
1) Fields / schema
- What fields are present in the inference audit log event today?
- Do events include request_id and customer-provided correlation IDs?
- Do events include: model, model_version, deployment, region, endpoint/route, response status code, latency, token counts, and error codes?
- Do events include caller identity (API key id / service account / user)?
- Do events include source IP / user agent (or equivalent) for audit trails?

2) Export / delivery
- Can exports be delivered to a customer-managed bucket (preferred) with customer-managed encryption keys?
- Is export cadence configurable (hourly/daily)?
- Is there an API to pull logs instead of pushing to object storage?
- Are exports JSON, CSV, or both?

3) Retention / backfill
- How long does Redwood retain audit logs in the control plane by default?
- Can Redwood backfill exports for a given window?

Impact
- Blocking Arcadia security/compliance sign-off for reference onboarding materials and their internal go-live checklist.
- Not a production outage; compliance enablement request.

Notes / context
- This came up after the 2025-05-13 security review call. Arcadia emphasized: no PHI in logs; logs must support their SIEM ingestion + audit evidence.
- Owner request: provide a short, customer-shareable schema description + sample event (sanitized), and confirm cadence/delivery options for their VPC deployment.

Attachments/links (internal)
- Fireflies: ff_2025-05-13_arcadia-health_security-review (timestamp ~31:40 audit logs)
- Gmail thread: markus_klein/thread_20250523_arcadia_metrics_validation_followup (mentions audit logging expectations as part of compliance checklist)

Requested by
- Arcadia: Security review + Platform Engineering
- Redwood: CS (Miguel) / SE (Simran) supporting reference onboarding
comments:
2025-05-14 10:12 PT — Miguel Santos (Reporter)
Created per Arcadia question list from security review. They want something they can paste into their compliance packet: (a) canonical field list, (b) export cadence, (c) delivery mechanism, (d) retention/backfill. Simran can you confirm current schema + what’s configurable for Private/VPC?

2025-05-14 14:37 PT — Simran Kaur (Assignee)
Pulled current audit event schema from Private control plane. At a high level: we log request lifecycle events at the API gateway + serving proxy boundary (not prompt/response content). We can share a sanitized JSONL sample.

Initial answers (will confirm details with Logan):
- Format: JSON Lines (one JSON object per event) compressed (gzip) when exported.
- Delivery: push to customer-managed S3-compatible bucket in the customer account for VPC deployments (Arcadia uses AWS). Supports SSE-KMS with customer-managed CMK.
- Cadence: default daily; can configure to hourly. “Near-real-time streaming” is not currently supported (no webhook), but hourly usually meets SIEM needs.
- Identity: includes Redwood workspace/org id, api_key_id, and (if sent) x-redwood-request-id / x-request-id passthrough; does not include end-user identity unless customer forwards it as a header we allowlist.
- Source IP: we log client_ip as observed at gateway. In VPC deployments behind private link / NAT, this may be the egress/NAT address; we can document caveat.
- Token counts: includes prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens when available; for some streaming disconnect cases counts can be partial.

Action: I’ll get Logan to confirm exact field names + retention/backfill behavior.

2025-05-15 09:05 PT — Logan Wright (Telemetry) — added as collaborator via Slack
Confirmed from current export pipeline in Private control plane.

Retention/backfill:
- Control plane retention: 30 days searchable in Console (Private) by default for Arcadia plan; can be extended via add-on (90/180) but usually not needed if exporting.
- Export pipeline keeps retrying failed deliveries for 7 days; we do not guarantee delivery beyond that window unless a backfill is requested.
- Backfill: supported on request for a bounded window (e.g., last 14 days) if logs still within retention; generates additional export objects with a backfill prefix.

Schema confirmation (field names):
- timestamp (RFC3339 UTC)
- event_type (request.received | request.completed | request.failed)
- request_id (Redwood-generated UUID)
- customer_request_id (if provided via header x-customer-request-id; allowlisted per deployment)
- workspace_id
- api_key_id
- route (e.g., /v1/chat/completions)
- model
- model_version (if pinned)
- deployment_mode (hosted | dedicated | private)
- region
- status_code
- error_code (if any)
- latency_ms
- prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens
- streaming (true/false)
- cache_hit (true/false when applicable)
- client_ip (best-effort; see NAT caveat)

Explicitly NOT included:
- prompt text, completions, embeddings payload, retrieved documents
- customer payload fields unless copied into allowlisted headers

We should be careful to tell them: customer_request_id requires allowlist and they must ensure it contains no PHI.

2025-05-15 11:22 PT — Simran Kaur
Thanks. I’ll draft customer-ready response including:
- Sample JSONL event (sanitized)
- Header allowlist note for x-customer-request-id
- Cadence options + delivery details (S3 + SSE-KMS)
- Retention/backfill defaults

Miguel: can you confirm who at Arcadia should receive the sample? (Security vs platform eng) and whether they need CSV as well (we don’t support CSV today).

2025-05-15 11:36 PT — Miguel Santos
Send to both: Priya (Security) + Dan (Platform). They asked specifically about CSV; please state JSONL only, but that it’s easy to ingest. Also call out that request_id is always present and can be used for correlation with Console traces.

2025-05-16 15:18 PT — Simran Kaur
Customer-facing reply sent (via email) with sample event and notes. Key points included:
- JSON Lines (.jsonl) gzipped objects delivered to their S3 bucket with SSE-KMS (customer CMK). We can provide bucket policy example.
- Daily export is default; configured hourly is available (recommended for SIEM). Exports are partitioned by date/hour.
- Confirmed field list and that no prompts/responses are logged.
- customer_request_id is supported via allowlisted header x-customer-request-id; Arcadia must ensure it contains no PHI.
- Console search retention 30 days; recommended to rely on S3 exports for long-term retention.
- Backfill available within retention window upon request.

Open item: Arcadia asked whether we can include "user_id" from their IdP. Current approach: pass through as allowlisted header (x-end-user-id) but we need to validate with Security (Naomi) that we’re comfortable documenting that pattern.

2025-05-19 10:02 PT — Naomi Feldman (Security/Claims review)
For compliance guidance: okay to document the “allowlisted header passthrough” pattern, with strong warning: Redwood will log header values as-is; customer is responsible for ensuring no PHI/regulated identifiers are included. Suggest naming it “customer_principal” and recommending opaque IDs.

Also recommend: do NOT suggest Redwood “captures IdP identity” natively; we do not integrate with their IdP for end-user attribution at this layer.

2025-05-20 09:44 PT — Simran Kaur
Aligned with Naomi. Follow-up email to Arcadia: clarified we do not pull IdP user identity; however, we can log an opaque customer principal identifier if they provide it as an allowlisted header. Included explicit caveat about PHI.

Miguel: anything else needed for the reference kickoff call today?

2025-05-23 13:08 PT — Miguel Santos
Arcadia confirmed this unblocks their compliance checklist. They opted for hourly exports and will proceed with configuring bucket + CMK. Marking resolved.

Follow-up task (internal): update Private deployment audit logging doc with:
- canonical field list
- NAT/client_ip caveat
- header allowlist guidance + PHI warning
(Do not include Arcadia name in docs.)
resolution: Provided Arcadia Health with a customer-shareable audit log schema (field list + sanitized JSONL sample), confirmed export delivery to customer-managed S3 with SSE-KMS (customer CMK), and enabled configurable export cadence (default daily; hourly available). Clarified retention/backfill behavior and documented the recommended pattern for customer-provided correlation IDs via allowlisted headers (with explicit ‘no PHI’ guidance). Customer confirmed requirements met and proceeded with hourly exports configuration.
